All edge tests pass.

Now let me re-run the fuzz batch (fresh seeds 400-700) plus the earlier ones to confirm no regressions after cleanup, and re-run scale tests. I'll run the fuzz in a background-ish manner with a time limit.

Also, let me consider adding predicate-with-variables coverage to the fuzz by writing an independent expression evaluator in the oracle... I think the hand tests cover the language well. But there's one more thing worth fuzzing: predicates over *recovered values* where the oracle evaluates the same expression through a second, independent implementation. Given limited value (I'd reuse my reading of the spec), I'll instead add a handful more hand tests for subtle cases:

1. `all` body referencing an enclosing `all` binding (lexical nesting) ✓ tested via nested same-name; let me also test an outer binding used inside the inner all (different names) — e.g. ["all","v",aa, ["all","w",["var","v"], ["eq",["add",["var","v"],["var","w"]], ...]]] → outer "v" visible inside ✓. My Forall copies the env with an added binding so outer bindings remain visible ✓.

2. `field`/`index` on `all` bindings ✓ (element of array of structs).

3. match with a pattern over a field of a struct inside an all binding ✓.

Let me add these to t_pred quickly to be safe.

Also worth testing: enum values with 4096 entries and the width-4 index ✓ (scale test used 512).

Let me add the nested-binding test.

cd /workspace/tmp && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='t_pred.py'; t=open(p).read()
t = t.replace('''    # null predicate means true
    (None, dict(), "READY"),
]''', '''    # outer bindings stay visible inside inner bindings
    (["all", "v", ["var", "aa"], ["all", "w", ["var", "v"],
      ["eq", ["add", ["var", "v"], ["var", "w"]], ["const", "I4", 5]]]],
     dict(aa=((2, 2, 2), (3, 3, 3))), "READY"),
    (["all", "v", ["var", "aa"], ["all", "w", ["var", "v"],
      ["eq", ["add", ["var", "v"], ["var", "w"]], ["const", "I4", 5]]]],
     dict(aa=((2, 2, 2), (3, 3, 4))), "FILTERED"),
    # sibling bindings never leak between predicate branches
    (["and", ["all", "v", ["var", "a"], ["eq", ["var", "v"], ["const", "I4", 1]]],
      ["all", "v", ["var", "a"], ["eq", ["var", "v"], ["const", "I4", 1]]]],
     dict(a=(1, 1, 1)), "READY"),
    # index/field of a bound element, then match on it
    (["all", "v", ["var", "aa"], ["match", ["var", "v"], "[0-3]"]], dict(), "READY"),
    # null predicate means true
    (None, dict(), "READY"),
]''')
open(p,'w').write(t)
PYEOF
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 t_pred.py 2>&1 | tail -6
